items.explanation: カ is the katakana for 'ka', the same sound as hiragana か. It is か without the small dash on the right.
items.mnemonic: か without its mosquito: only the arm swinging down in a karate chop.
items.culture_note: カ developed from the kanji 加.

items.explanation: キ is the katakana for 'ki', the same sound as hiragana き. It is き without the hook at the bottom.
items.mnemonic: Two crossbars on a slanted post: the frame of a kite.
items.culture_note: キ developed from the kanji 幾.

items.explanation: ク is the katakana for 'ku', the same sound as hiragana く. Do not confuse it with ケ (a line crosses to the right) or タ (an extra stroke inside).
items.mnemonic: く wearing a small cap: the cuckoo put on a hat.
items.culture_note: ク developed from the kanji 久.

items.explanation: ケ is the katakana for 'ke', the same sound as hiragana け. Its crossbar pokes out to the right, which is how you tell it from ク.
items.mnemonic: A capital K leaning back and missing one leg.
items.culture_note: ケ developed from the kanji 介.

items.explanation: コ is the katakana for 'ko', the same sound as hiragana こ.
items.mnemonic: A box open on the left: a cozy corner.
items.culture_note: コ developed from the kanji 己. コーヒー came from the Dutch koffie: for over two centuries the Dutch were the only Europeans allowed to trade with Japan, from the small island of Dejima in Nagasaki.
